title: Live Like Updates
summary: Extend durable like counters with coalesced Pub/Sub updates to millions of subscribed WebSocket clients.
narrative:
Extend level-33's Facebook Like Counter so people watching an open feed see counts change without refreshing. Keep its write path: conditional NoSQL records keyed by (post_id, user_id), effective like/unlike events in a post-partitioned log, Stream Processor aggregation and cached counts. Unlike deletes a record and own-like checks remain point reads. At ~5 B likes/day, about 58 K/s average and ~500 K/s peak, celebrity posts still need batched counters and idempotent processing; the new challenge is broadcasting those counts to millions of screens.

Each open browser or app holds a WebSocket and subscribes only to post ids currently on screen. With ~100 M concurrent connections and ~100 K connections per socket server, plan for ~1,000 socket servers. A single hot post can have millions of simultaneous viewers. Stream Processors coalesce deltas over ~1–2 s and publish at most about one 'post X now has N likes' update per second per post to its Pub/Sub topic. One publish fans out to thousands of socket servers, each pushing to its local subscribers; nobody needs 10 K separate updates/s for a celebrity post.

Keep like API servers independent of socket server membership: they append to the log and never call socket servers directly. Pub/Sub delivers aggregated counts to redundant WebSocket Servers, and redundant Stream Processors recover from the replicated log. Replicate durable like and counter state, repair partial record/event publication failures, and apply batches idempotently before committing offsets. Counts are eventually consistent; clients can accept newer count versions and resubscribe after reconnecting. Optionally read the latest count from Cache when a socket subscribes, and monitor connection churn and end-to-end update freshness.

functional: Persist conditional like records, publish effective transitions and aggregate counters in NoSQL and Cache as in level-33
Read cached counts through the HTTP API and subscribe WebSocket clients to on-screen post ids
Coalesce updates over ~1–2 s and publish approximately once/s per post to its Pub/Sub topic
Fan each topic out to the socket servers with interested local viewers
Resubscribe after reconnecting and use count versions to avoid regressing the display
nonFunctional: Support ~100 M concurrent sockets and hot posts with millions of viewers
Keep count updates eventually consistent and bounded in frequency
Survive a WebSocket Server or Stream Processor instance failure with reconnect and replay
constraints: Never connect the like API directly to WebSocket Servers
All Stream Processor to WebSocket Server paths must pass through Pub/Sub
Connect WebSocket Servers to Pub/Sub; publish coalesced count snapshots rather than every like
Preserve unique like records and idempotent counter batches; replicate the event log and durable stores
capacity: ~100 M connections / ~100 K per socket server ≈1,000 servers
Millions of simultaneous viewers on one hot post; coalesce ~1–2 s windows and cap each post near 1 update/s
Inherited write load: ~5 B likes/day ≈58 K/s average, ~500 K/s peak; a hot post can receive ~10 K likes/s
specs.tradeoff: Coalesced count snapshots reduce publish and rendering work but add a second or two of staleness. Topic subscriptions avoid broadcasting irrelevant posts, at the cost of subscription churn as users scroll. Pub/Sub decouples writers from socket placement; reconnection still needs a fresh count and resubscription.
specs.bonus: Connect WebSocket Servers → Cache for the current count on subscription and add Monitoring for socket churn and update freshness.

topologyRules.message: Don't have the like API call socket servers — publish once and let Pub/Sub fan out.
Deliver aggregated counts through Pub/Sub before reaching WebSocket Servers.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two WebSocket Servers so clients can reconnect after a failure.
Run at least two Stream Processors for count aggregation.
Connect WebSocket Servers to Pub/Sub for per-post fan-out.

hints: Rebuild level-33: Client → Load Balancer → Web Server, then Web Server → NoSQL, → Cache and → Message Queue → Stream Processor. Connect the processor to NoSQL and Cache for batched counts.
Add Client → WebSocket Server for subscriptions. Publish coalesced counts with Stream Processor → Pub/Sub → WebSocket Server; do not wire the like API to sockets.

Use two Web Servers, two Stream Processors and two WebSocket Servers. Both processors reach NoSQL, Cache and Pub/Sub; Pub/Sub reaches both socket servers. Each Web Server reaches NoSQL, the queue, Cache and Monitoring. Add each WebSocket Server → Cache for the initial count.
